verdict.tagline: Addictive store management buried under severe bugs and clumsy workers.
for_you_if: you enjoy building and expanding a retail business
you can handle repetitive late-stage gameplay loops
not_for_you_if: you expect reliable multiplayer features on release
you are sensitive to save file corruption issues
you struggle with tiny unscalable text sizes

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players note that the grind intensifies later while employee AI struggles to maintain efficient restocking routines.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the AI for restocker employees as inefficient, noting that workers leave half-empty boxes on shelves, abandon tasks midway, or fail to complete restocking loops.

citations.review_text:
While I do recommend this game, I will also advise persons interested in this game to wait until it is deep discount.  It is not a finished game by FAR.  There are a lot of bugs that are just annoying.  I have noticed that a lot of the time these bugs occur in multiplayer. Single player has been pretty solid.
     Another reason I say wait for a discount is because the AI staff members that run stock are quite dumb.  An example being, that if the stock person has a box with 1 or 2 items in it, they will put them on the shelf, but then never go back to grab the rest of that stock to fill the shelf.  If a customer comes in right behind them and grabs the items.  The shelf will sit empty for a while without human intervention.
A minor detail here but the traffic in the world is pretty bad.  Cars come slamming to a halt at red lights and end up with the rear wheels in the air momentarily.  That just seems sloppy for a "finished game" or "Not early Access"
This game feels like a close to release beta.  I guess that is what digital game streaming has come down to though these days.
Still has a lot of replay value and micro management to keep someone entertained.

I love this game especially with every new updates it receives, and I also enjoy there is DLC for pretty cheap to add more to the game so I feel like i might never run out of content. 

I only have a couple complaints.
1. The staff's AI especially the restockers, I wish I could order them to do specifique thing's, Once the store gets too large the restocking seem's to just never end. I find if I could position one to only restock produce and another at fridge. I WOULD LOVE to tell one to just restock from the loading area into the storage. It just takes them to long to stalk up on the shelfs they never get to the boxes outside. I find being able to order them around and maybe a leveling feature so they get better over time without needing to boost. These features would remove a pile of work off the player and be able to focus on just enjoying the game all together or other thing's like delivery. To which, I wish I could hire a staff for that as well. 
2. I wish that when it come's to getting the products out in the map that I could make a list of what you need and that once you've put the box in the car, etc. That it would get checked out or removed from the list. It just take to longs to memories what I need and go back and forth because I don't remember or realized I bought the wrong thing but i like the feature or getting out to get it yourself for cheaper it's just infuriating at times.

Needs better tutorials. The workers you hire just stand there. Especially the re-stocker. He'll work for a moment and then just stops and leave the rest of the work for YOU to do. You can adjust the toggles with a full warehouse and he'll stand there and daydream all day!!! Even if you help him while he works, he will then stop. This is a long going issue that will probably never be fixed. It is also extremely glitchy with other things as well. Online orders don't appear and then you will get a notification that they expired. You'll have a line of people going through your register and while your handling business, you'll see that your helper isn't helping the customer at the self checkout. It's just looking into space. By the time you get a chance to fix the developer coded buggy issue, the customer walks out the door, missed opportunity! Beware before you buy. 

PS. There is no explanation on how to operate the scale or know what it is asking for you to do. You have to go on youtube to figure it out.

Easy Chill Relaxing Supermarket Sim is one of the best simulators I have played lots of it and enjoy it loads it is better with friends btw it is in early access so there is the odd bug or two but either way its still great

One of the bugs I experienced is the re stockers keep not stocking even though I ordered things looks like a bug to do with the player picking up the box they was going for or something similiar therefore interfering with the Re stockers path finder

I do really enjoy this game, it gives a more relaxed alternative than my other games. There are a few features I think could be fun to add, I personally enjoy being able to automate as much as possible so some of these will not be to the taste of those that enjoy the manual handling. 

- Please fix the baker
- Allow ice cream stalls outside (but not far from) the store
- Pallet truck/dolly to help move deliveries into storage, or even from storage to shop floor (be nice if stockers could use them) 
- Shelf/stocker behaviour that allows half boxes to be refilled, I personally hate having 4 half used boxes of product. Would be nice to code stockers not to put half boxes on regular storage racks, or have them specify a rack for part boxes that they can label and unlabel as its used. My thought is a rack for full boxes of stock, the part boxes are then priority use in a different rack. 
- From last point, maybe a discount bin for half boxes, any products get sold at 90% just as a sacrifice to keep nice orderly storage.
- stockers being assigned to different item types like shelf or fridge products, if one type of product is struggling. 
- online delivery staff, they place completed bags on a specific table so you can just deliver them.
- delivery staff to work with or instead of above
- Half price from stores is good incentive but more of a reason to use cars? 
- upgrade staff to work faster permanently or daily from the computer instead of chasing and boosting them
- Staff who can order stock
- More options when it comes to staff behaviour
- options to toggle these in case people still want that effort and grind, I just personally enjoy the shop growth and being able to step back to watch it all happen. 

Sorry this ended up long. This isnt to say all these need to be in the game, or that everyone will want these. Its just things that pop into my head while I play and think about what could be added, if those things would work for this game. Otherwise, really enjoyable…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game becomes repetitive and grindy in the later stages, requiring significant time investments to afford store expansions.

citations.review_text: It is a fun job simulator, as of 63 hours I am starting to feel it getting repetitive.

Super addicting. I am a fan of simulation games, for example Sim City, and this really satisfies that itch! I can play it easily on my Macbook Air. 

I wish there were more tools that you could unlock as you progress in stage, it seems like it may start getting repetitive soon. But I still enjoy and highly recommend this game!

Really bad UX. Too many bugs. Basic features like sorting and bulk pricing/discount updates still missing. Driving mechanic becomes important part after a certain point but it's so poorly implemented. Weird limiations with too many product boxes. And lots of other frustrating elements.

Game starts feeling like a chore after a while. It also started feeling frustrating eventually. Dev needs to focus on more quality of life updates to make the game more stable and convenient and remove any unneceesary grind that doesn't feel rewarding.

It is a fun little game, but gets very repetitive fast. Realistically you've seen everything after the first few hours, then it's just a game of saving up money to buy more product licenses, to expand the store and repeat. Game gets very slow after a certain point, you have to grind for weeks to save up enough to be able to afford an expansion. Add to that that the restockers are extremely slow and you have to do the restocking yourself if you want to move forward. If you want to save money you have to drive from wholesale to wholesale, eating up even more time. Now that one day is effectively one full hour and there's basically no progress anymore, I've decided to uninstall this game for good.

I do recommend it, the price is okay and you can have a few hours worth of fun with it. But don't try to push it too far, when it starts getting too grindy just stop and play something else. The grind only gets worse in the later game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that DLC items lack integration with wholesale discount stores, leaving players to pay market prices for them.

citations.review_text: really sucks how the devs ruined such a good game, i highly advise against buying this game since the devs would rather prioritize 30$ dlcs than adding them to the base game for free considering theyre such small things. if youre looking for a different supermarket game megastore simulator is great

Very addicting and fun, probably my favorite Simulator game of all time. I wholeheartedly recommend buying the base game, but I strongly advise against purchasing any of the DLC content:

The game has a wholesale shop mechanic, where you can shop at specialised stores to get items with a massive discount (50%), but NONE of the DLC-specific items are tied to any wholesale stores. They don't have their own  stores either

This feels like a massive oversight, and you can feel the impact of lacking those wholesale stores when you're stocking up on 300$ electronics. The profit margins when you're only buying at market price aren't worth the real money you'll have to spend on the DLCs

claims.claim: Reviewers note that updates break mods and custom content created for the game.

citations.review_text:
Devs constantly break the mods that made the game fun to share and stream.
The value added is not proportional.

I LOVED this game, and would come back to it every couple months to sink a week or so in.

But man it's gone downhill. Updates feel shoddy and AI made, things constantly not working. The Delivery system feels so bad in the game, the DLCs are minor updates that don't really work and cost money. 

Really sad to see how bad this game has gotten. A genuine "was better before full release" tragic tale.

The game is really good, but you should add more licenses for new products, because that’s what keeps players motivated and excited to continue playing.

You should also make it easier for content creators to work with the game, since with every update, custom contents stop working. That becomes frustrating for people who invest their time into making the game richer and more enjoyable for everyone.

Looking forward to hearing your feedback and seeing future updates.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the employee cap at six restockers as insufficient for managing larger store sizes and higher inventory volumes.

citations.review_text:
HUGE WASTE OF POTENTIAL

Honestly I had a lot of fun in the beginning but it doesn't take long for the fatal flaws and poor design decisions to completely overtake the experience. 

Once you get to around level 50, it basically becomes impossible to get anywhere because for whatever reason, the devs decided to cap the amount of restockers you can hire at 6. On top of that neither you the player nor the restockers can carry more than one box at a time, making restocking, organizing and inventory a massive drag. Would be an easy fix for the devs to just add more restockers or a trolley of some sort to carry more boxes or straight to storage delivery OR REALLY ANYTHING and make this game actually playable. 

Quality of life is very poor overall, just again more decisions that logically make no sense despite the scale of store the game intends on your reaching. 

Such as daily market price changes for products, which is great, until you realize there is no way to filter the products list to find what items changed price. Instead you have to scroll through the ENTIRE list to find the ones that changed price. This seems easy enough at the start, but when you get over 200 products, it literally becomes an eyesore. 

The idea of wholesale stores is fun, get items half price if you go pick them up yourself. But again you are not given the tools necessary to actually sustain your store with wholesale. The biggest vehicle you can get is a truck which very quickly becomes obsolete. Again logically you'd think you'd eventually get to upgrade to a box truck or something but no. This is where the box carrying limitations also kick in. You have to individually purchase each product box and carry it to the truck. When you need to purchase like 50 boxes, it gets old REAL QUICK. Then of course you have to take it all back to the store to be unloaded and stored, then comes the restocking grind all over again. 

There are lots more little things that just add more friction t…

I don't understand why the received goods should stand front of the customer door in the way of the customers. There are only more and more goods coming in, as the restockers can't keep up, there are only 6 restockers and goods should not be out on the street.

And maybe the just 6 restockers is why I thinking on stop plat Supermarked Simulator?

The bigger your store becomes, the more tedious keeping stock in your store room becomes. You get to pick between half a dozen trips in a pick up truck or losing quite a bit of profit by ordering it delivered.

This is easily fixable by either adding a larger vehicle, like a box truck, or allowing customization of settings to reduce the fee of delivery.

I was looking forward to the update that let you disable licenses but, people still come in looking for items in your unlocked licenses, they just don't complain about them not being in the store. It also makes it very difficult to do things like run a bakery only as the bakery items don't really make much in the way of profit so, even a couple of employees will put you at weeks or months of saving up for the next upgrade.

I really want to love this game, there's such a good foundation but right now, it just gets too tedious to be fun and I'm someone who enjoys a certain amount of tedium in my games.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that DLC packs add product skins and minor updates while being viewed as overpriced or buggy.

citations.review_text: Really enjoy the main game! Lots of products to organize. I wish I could check my inventory when outside of the shop. Would not recommend buying the DLCs aside from essentials as they are buggy.

I played Supermarket Simulator throughout its beta and absolutely loved it. It was one of those rare indie games that I couldn’t wait to recommend. The gameplay loop was addictive, the steady updates were exciting, and I was looking forward to supporting the full release.

Unfortunately, the launch completely changed my opinion.

Instead of simply releasing the finished game, the developer immediately introduced seven paid DLC packs, ranging from $1.99 to $6.99, that add nothing but product skins. Individually they may seem inexpensive, but together they create the feeling that content has been carved out to be sold separately on day one.

For a game that built its reputation during Early Access, this left a bad taste in my mouth. It feels less like supporting an indie developer and more like the beginning of a microtransaction strategy that I simply don’t want to encourage.

The core game is still enjoyable, but the monetization has fundamentally changed how I view it. What was once a must-buy has become an avoid for me—not because of the gameplay, but because of the direction the developer chose to take.

I hope the developer reconsiders this approach, because there is still a great game underneath it.

I LOVED this game, and would come back to it every couple months to sink a week or so in.

But man it's gone downhill. Updates feel shoddy and AI made, things constantly not working. The Delivery system feels so bad in the game, the DLCs are minor updates that don't really work and cost money. 

Really sad to see how bad this game has gotten. A genuine "was better before full release" tragic tale.
